status: Fixed in source and verified through the current frozen runner; formal closeout remains a separate state
area: Governed commit auto-stage / framework claim scope / cross-task ownership
finding: isFrameworkGeneratedArtifactAllowed admitted any path matching a claimed scope through pathMatchesTaskScope, so a directory-shaped framework temporary claim inherited every path beneath it. When the claim declared a directory such as .atm/ or .atm/history/evidence/, governed auto-stage swept another known task's governance history file into the commit candidate set, including untracked ones. The cross-task mutation guard then correctly refused the commit and named a path the operator had never staged; the wrapper rolled the index back, so the operator afterwards observed an empty git diff --cached and read the refusal as a pre-commit admission defect rather than a staging-scope defect.
expectedBehavior: A directory scope grants reach inside a claim; it never transfers authority over another task's governance history. Directory-scope inheritance must not admit .atm/history/{evidence,task-events,tasks} paths owned by a different known task. Naming a path exactly in the claim remains a deliberate authority act and stays admitted. Generated release surfaces such as release/** and packages/cli/dist/** are not task history and keep their existing directory semantics. Ownership must be resolved through the single cross-task owner seam so governed staging and cross-task admission cannot drift apart.
evidenceOrRepro: Red reproduction ran the real autoStageFrameworkClaimFiles with apply=false against throwaway git fixtures. With a claim of exactly .atm/git-hooks/pre-commit and .atm/git-hooks/pre-push the foreign untracked receipt was correctly excluded, but with a claim of .atm/history/evidence/ or .atm/ the foreign receipt entered the candidate set. tests/cli/framework-auto-stage-foreign-task-history.test.ts failed before the repair on 'a directory-scoped claim must not sweep a foreign task history path into the governed candidate set' and passes after it. The repair exports resolveTaskHistoryOwnerTaskId from packages/core/src/broker/cross-task-mutation-guard.ts, makes detectCrossTaskMutation consume that same seam, and adds an optional ownerScope argument to isFrameworkGeneratedArtifactAllowed that is supplied by autoStageFrameworkClaimFiles, inspectFrameworkScopedUnstagedCommit, and commit-framework-branch. Live-repository admission results were identical before and after the extraction, so the guard refactor is behaviour-preserving. At the time of writing no released or active lock in .atm/runtime/locks declares a directory scope over .atm/history, so the defect was latent rather than actively firing.
containment: No foreign residue was cleaned and no foreign staged bytes were absorbed while investigating. The repair is preventive: it stops a future directory-scoped claim from sweeping foreign governance history into a commit, and it does not reduce existing worktree residue. Claims taken while this item is open should list exact file paths rather than directory scopes; the safe existing idiom for a task's own evidence is a scope bound to that task id, for example .atm/history/evidence/ATM-FRAMEWORK-TEMP-<own-task>.*.
followUp: Frozen-runner publication is now verified: source repair 49fea0eaf5285dfe2eedb2a86b71569ddf0148cf is an ancestor of the current sealed runner, whose sourceSeal.valid=true and syncRequired=false. The focused regression node --strip-types tests/cli/framework-auto-stage-foreign-task-history.test.ts passed again against that runner generation. Formal task-card closeout is not claimed by this quickfix. The staging provenance of the originally reported 2026-08-30T14:46:42Z refusal remains unavailable: the commit-attempt snapshot .atm/runtime/git-commit-attempts/codex-gpt-5.4-mini__no-task.json proves the foreign receipt was present in the live index at hook time through its liveIndexResidueRollback list, and that HEAD did not advance, but those snapshots are overwritten per actor and task, and the claim scope in force at that moment was already released, so whether auto-stage or a concurrent lane placed the path in the shared index cannot be determined from surviving evidence.
